question.text: Which of the following is a DEFINITIVE AGREEMENT for an AIF investment into an investee company?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.5 (Definitive Agreements), definitive agreements are the set of binding agreements between the investee company and the AIF. These include: (i) Share Subscription/Purchase Agreement and (ii) Shareholders' Agreement (SHA). PPM is an investor-facing offering document; teaser/CIM is pre-deal marketing; trust deed governs the AIF trust, not the investee. The Trap: PPM governs AIF-to-LP relationship, not AIF-to-investee. Teasers are pre-binding marketing. Trust deeds are internal to the AIF structure. Cross-Exam Context: Definitive agreements tested in XIX-A and XV — the SHA/SSA pair is the universal answer. Manager's Pro-Tip: A common failure: Share Subscription Agreement provisions bind only the company; to bind existing shareholders, you MUST have an SHA. Check that both exist before wiring subscription amounts.
